WITH base AS (
  SELECT m.department AS department, i.income_id
  FROM income i
  JOIN member mem ON i.link_to_member = mem.member_id
  JOIN major m ON mem.link_to_major = m.major_id
),
dept AS (
  SELECT department, COUNT(*) AS cnt
  FROM base
  GROUP BY department
),
tot AS (
  SELECT SUM(cnt) AS total FROM dept
),
shares AS (
  SELECT d.department, d.cnt, CAST(d.cnt AS REAL) / t.total AS share
  FROM dept d
  CROSS JOIN tot t
),
avg_share AS (
  SELECT AVG(share) AS a FROM shares
),
kept AS (
  SELECT s.department, s.cnt, s.share
  FROM shares s
  CROSS JOIN avg_share a
  WHERE s.share > a.a
)
SELECT
  SUM(k.cnt) AS total_count,
  AVG(k.share) AS avg_share,
  AVG(k.share - a.a) AS avg_share_deviation
FROM kept k
CROSS JOIN avg_share a;

assumptions.assumption: Income rows are kept only when the income's member exists in member and that member's link_to_major matches an existing major; inner joins drop the rest.
Departments are grouped by major.department as stored; a NULL department forms its own single group rather than being dropped.

The 'average share' used for the threshold and for the deviation is the plain average over all departments (before filtering), not over only the kept departments, since averaging deviations from the kept-department average would always yield 0.
If no department exceeds the average, the query returns one row with NULL values (SUM and AVG over no rows).
